summary.text: A permutation is a rearrangement of a finite set, a function that moves each member to a new place.
The number of permutations of n distinct objects is n factorial, the product of the first n positive integers.
Anagrams are permutations of letters, and studying permutations as substitutions led to the notion of a group in algebra.

facts.label: How many
facts.value: n distinct objects can be permuted in n factorial ways

facts.label: Partial permutations
facts.value: Ordered sequences of k distinct elements of a set

facts.label: Derangement
facts.value: A permutation with no fixed points

items.prompt: A puzzle asks you to rearrange the letters of the word "listen" to spell "silent". What kind of thing have you made?

options.label: A fixed point of the word
A single cycle with one letter

items.explain: Anagrams are examples of permutations of sequences of letters.

items.prompt: After shuffling a row of numbered cards, card 4 is still sitting in position 4. What is such an element called?
items.explain: An element taken to itself is a fixed point. A derangement is a whole permutation with no fixed points, not a single element.

items.prompt: You swap exactly two cards in a row and leave every other card where it was. What is this kind of shuffle called?
items.explain: A permutation exchanging two elements and leaving the rest fixed is a transposition. A derangement would move every element.

items.prompt: A coach picks 2 players from a squad of 5 and lists them in order. What are such ordered lists of distinct members called?
items.explain: The ordered sequences of k distinct elements of a set are called k-permutations, or partial permutations.

items.prompt: You apply one shuffle to a deck, then a second shuffle. Another time you apply the second shuffle first. In general, what do you find?

options.label: The two results are always identical
The first result is always the reverse of the second
The results match only if the deck is small
The two results are typically different

items.explain: Composition of permutations is in general not commutative, so applying them in a different order typically gives a different result.

items.prompt: A librarian has n different books and wants to know how many orders they can stand in on a shelf. Which expression gives it?
items.explain: The number of permutations of n distinct objects is the product of the first n positive integers, called n factorial.
